scenario: Greeting someone for the first time
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Informal greeting used to say hello and goodbye.
Subject pronoun for the first person singular.
Subject pronoun for the second person singular, familiar form.
In 'piacere di conoscerti' it means 'pleased to meet you'.
Preposition indicating a relation, here 'to meet you'.
Verb in -ere, here in the infinitive after 'di'.
Second person singular of the verb 'stare' (to be, to feel).
Adverb of manner, standard answer to 'Come stai?'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ciao! Io sono Marco.
dialogue.translation: Hello! I am Marco.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ciao, Marco! Piacere di conoscerti. Io sono Sophie.
dialogue.translation: Hello, Marco! Nice to meet you. I am Sophie.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Piacere mio! Come stai?
dialogue.translation: The pleasure is mine! How are you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bene, grazie! E tu?
dialogue.translation: Well, thanks! And you?

scenario: Asking where something is in a store
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Dov'è il reparto frutta?
dialogue.translation: Where is the fruit section?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: È qui, signore, a destra.
dialogue.translation: It's here, sir, on the right.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E la cassa, è lì?
dialogue.translation: And the checkout, is it there?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, la cassa è in fondo, dopo il pane.
dialogue.translation: No, the checkout is at the back, after the bread.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Grazie!
dialogue.translation: Thank you!

scenario: Ordering a drink at a café
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Very frequent verb, used to order (prendere un caffè).
Common modal verb, often used in the conditional (vorrei) for politeness.
Invariable masculine noun, typical drink at the bar.
Feminine noun, often accompanied by 'minerale' or 'naturale'.
Demonstrative determiner, very frequent, agrees with the noun (questo caffè).
Form of the verb 'costare' (to cost), very frequent to ask a price.
Adverb of time, often used to link actions.
Very common preposition, used to indicate accompaniment.
Coordinating conjunction, very frequent to contrast two ideas.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, vorrei prendere un caffè.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I would like to have a coffee.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Certo. E poi, vuole qualcosa da mangiare?
dialogue.translation: Of course. And then, would you like something to eat?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No, grazie. Ma vorrei anche un'acqua naturale.
dialogue.translation: No, thank you. But I would also like a still water.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ecco il caffè e l'acqua. Quanto costa?
dialogue.translation: Here is the coffee and the water. How much does it cost?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Questo caffè costa due euro, e l'acqua un euro. Con questo, fa tre euro.
dialogue.translation: This coffee costs two euros, and the water one euro. With this, that makes three euros.

key_phrases.translation: I would like to have a coffee

scenario: Buying a ticket at a station
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, vorrei un biglietto per Roma.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I would like a ticket to Rome.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Certo. Che ora? C'è un treno alle dieci.
dialogue.translation: Of course. What time? There is a train at ten.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quando arriva a Roma?
dialogue.translation: When does it arrive in Rome?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Parte ora e arriva dopo due ore.
dialogue.translation: It leaves now and arrives after two hours.

scenario: Checking in at a hotel reception
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buonasera, ho una prenotazione. Mi chiamo Marie.
dialogue.translation: Good evening, I have a reservation. My name is Marie.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Benvenuta! Qual è il suo nome, per favore?
dialogue.translation: Welcome! What is your name, please?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Marie Dupont. Ho prenotato una camera per una notte.
dialogue.translation: Marie Dupont. I booked a room for one night.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfetto. Ecco la chiave. Il numero della camera è il 204.
dialogue.translation: Perfect. Here is the key. The room number is 204.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Grazie mille. Dov'è la camera? La trovo facilmente?
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much. Where is the room? Can I find it easily?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sì, è al secondo piano. Arriva con l'ascensore, è molto facile.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's on the second floor. Take the elevator, it's very easy.

scenario: Meeting a new neighbor
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Used to introduce oneself collectively or to say 'it's us'.
Agrees in gender and number. Here in masculine singular.
Possessive adjective, agreeing with the masculine singular noun.
1st person plural of the present tense.
It is placed before or after the verb.
1st person singular of the present tense.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno! Siamo i nuovi vicini, io sono Marco e lei è mia moglie, Anna.
dialogue.translation: Good morning! We are the new neighbors, I am Marco and she is my wife, Anna.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ah, piacere! Io sono Carla. Benvenuti. Da quanto tempo abitate qui?
dialogue.translation: Ah, pleased to meet you! I am Carla. Welcome. How long have you been living here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Abitiamo al terzo piano, da una settimana. E voi, abitate qui da molto?
dialogue.translation: We live on the third floor, for a week. And you, have you lived here long?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sì, anche io abito al terzo piano, ma al primo. Che coincidenza! E perché vi siete trasferiti?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I also live on the third floor, but on the first. What a coincidence! And why did you move?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perché abbiamo trovato un lavoro qui. Spero di conoscerti meglio presto!
dialogue.translation: Because we found a job here. I hope to get to know you better soon!

key_phrases.translation: How long have you been living here?
I hope to get to know you better

scenario: Asking the time on the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Attention: 'ora' is also an adverb meaning 'now'.
Essential for telling time: 'è l'una', 'sono le due'.
Indefinite article, used for the time: 'è l'una' (it's one o'clock).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Scusi, sa che ora è?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sì, sono le due e mezza.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's two thirty.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Grazie. E il treno parte alle tre?
dialogue.translation: Thank you. And does the train leave at three?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, alle quattro, in ritardo.
dialogue.translation: No, at four, late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ah, allora ho tempo. Grazie ancora!
dialogue.translation: Ah, then I have time. Thanks again!

scenario: At the doctor for a basic checkup
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Irregular verb, very frequent, used here for 'to see the doctor'.
Used to ask questions about health status.
Used in 'avere male a' to express pain.
Frequent, used in expressions of pain.
Used to respond 'sto bene' (I am well).
Irregular verb, used for 'dare una medicina'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, dottore. Oggi voglio vedere come sto.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, doctor. Today I want to see how I am.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ciao! Come ti senti? Hai male alla testa?
dialogue.translation: Hi! How do you feel? Do you have a headache?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sì, un po'. Ma quando prendo una medicina, sto più bene.
dialogue.translation: Yes, a little. But when I take medicine, I feel better.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Va bene. Ti do una ricetta. Quando torni domani?
dialogue.translation: Alright. I'll give you a prescription. When do you come back tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Grazie, dottore. Oggi non ho più male. Arrivederci!
dialogue.translation: Thank you, doctor. Today I no longer have pain. Goodbye!

scenario: Paying at a supermarket checkout
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Very frequent verb, used here in the expression 'to queue' (fare la fila).
Feminine singular. Refers to the supermarket checkout.
Regular verb in -are. Often followed by 'per' or an object complement.
Masculine noun. Used for the total amount to pay.
Here, 'carta' means 'bank card'. It can also mean 'paper'.
Loanword from English, used in Italian to refer to the debit card.
Masculine noun. The receipt given after payment.
Feminine singular. Refers to the shopping bag.
Adverb of time. Note: already seen in the previous list, but here used with a different contextual meaning.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Devo fare la coda alla cassa per pagare.
dialogue.translation: I have to queue at the checkout to pay.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Il totale è venti euro. Paga in contanti o con carta?
dialogue.translation: The total is twenty euros. Do you pay in cash or by card?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pago con il bancomat, per favore.
dialogue.translation: I pay with my debit card, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ecco il suo scontrino. Vuole una borsa?
dialogue.translation: Here is your receipt. Would you like a bag?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sì, grazie. Poi prendo la borsa e vado.
dialogue.translation: Yes, thanks. Then I'll take the bag and go.

scenario: Calling a friend to make simple plans
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Irregular verb, very useful for plans.
Masculine noun, same meaning as in Spanish.
Subject pronoun for the first person plural.
Contracted article, already seen but here in another context.
3rd person singular of 'andare', used in 'va bene'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ciao! Domani vuoi andare al cinema con me?
dialogue.translation: Hi! Do you want to go to the cinema with me tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sì, volentieri! Ma dove ci troviamo?
dialogue.translation: Yes, gladly! But where do we meet?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Possiamo andare al cinema alle sette. Va bene?
dialogue.translation: We can go to the cinema at seven. Is that okay?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfetto! Allora noi ci vediamo lì. A domani!
dialogue.translation: Perfect! Then we'll see each other there. See you tomorrow!

key_phrases.translation: do you want to go to the cinema?

scenario: Describing your family to someone
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Feminine, used for family in a broad sense.
Agrees in gender and number: grande/grandi.
Agrees in gender and number: piccolo/piccoli/piccola/piccole.
Auxiliary verb, very frequent. Conjugated: ho, hai, ha...
Intransitive verb, often followed by 'a' or 'in' for place.
Adverb of place; equivalent to 'here' in English.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ciao! Questa è la mia famiglia: mio padre, mia madre, mio fratello e mia sorella.
dialogue.translation: Hi! This is my family: my father, my mother, my brother, and my sister.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Che bello! Hai un fratello e una sorella? Quanti anni hanno?
dialogue.translation: How nice! Do you have a brother and a sister? How old are they?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sì, mio fratello ha vent'anni e mia sorella è piccola, ha dieci anni.
dialogue.translation: Yes, my brother is twenty years old and my sister is little, she is ten years old.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: E i tuoi genitori? Sono grandi o giovani?
dialogue.translation: And your parents? Are they old or young?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mio padre ha cinquant'anni, mia madre è più giovane. Vivono qui, vicino a me.
dialogue.translation: My father is fifty years old, my mother is younger. They live here, near me.

scenario: Asking for directions in the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Scusi, per andare alla stazione, quale strada devo prendere?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, to go to the station, which street should I take?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Vada sempre dritto, poi giri a destra.
dialogue.translation: Go straight ahead, then turn right.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A destra o a sinistra?
dialogue.translation: To the right or to the left?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A destra, subito dopo il bar. Non è difficile, lo sa tutto qui.
dialogue.translation: To the right, right after the bar. It's not difficult, everyone here knows it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Grazie, spero di trovare la strada senza chiedere ancora.
dialogue.translation: Thank you, I hope to find the street without asking again.

scenario: On a bus asking the driver for help
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; used to get off a vehicle.
Feminine noun; designates the bus stop.
Polite form to address a man.

dialogue.speaker: A (passager)
dialogue.text: Signore, per favore, devo scendere alla prossima fermata?
dialogue.translation: Sir, please, do I have to get off at the next stop?

dialogue.speaker: B (chauffeur)
dialogue.text: Sì, la prossima fermata è qui. Ma questo autobus non si ferma qui.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the next stop is here. But this bus does not stop here.

dialogue.speaker: A (passager)
dialogue.text: Ah, come posso fare? Mi può aiutare?
dialogue.translation: Ah, what can I do? Can you help me?

dialogue.speaker: B (chauffeur)
dialogue.text: Certo, scenda alla prossima fermata e prenda il prossimo autobus.
dialogue.translation: Of course, get off at the next stop and take the next bus.

dialogue.speaker: A (passager)
dialogue.text: Grazie mille!
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much!

key_phrases.translation: Do I have to get off at the next stop?

scenario: Introducing a colleague at work
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Often used with 'come ti chiami' but here for introducing.
In 'piacere di conoscerti' = nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, questo è il mio nuovo collega, Marco.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, this is my new colleague, Marco.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Piacere, Marco. Qual è il tuo nome completo?
dialogue.translation: Nice to meet you, Marco. What is your full name?

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Il mio nome è Marco Rossi. Lavoro nell'ufficio di Milano.
dialogue.translation: My name is Marco Rossi. I work in the Milan office.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Anche io lavoro a Milano. Dove sta il tuo ufficio?
dialogue.translation: I also work in Milan. Where is your office?

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Il mio ufficio sta al terzo piano. Piacere di conoscerti!
dialogue.translation: My office is on the third floor. Nice to meet you!

scenario: Leaving a voicemail message
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Auxiliary and main verb; very frequent.
Subject pronoun, often omitted in Italian.
Attention: already in the exclusion list? Here used as 'later'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ciao, sono Maria. Non posso rispondere ora.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I'm Maria. I can't answer now.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ciao Maria, sono io, Luca. Ti chiamo per un messaggio.
dialogue.translation: Hello Maria, it's me, Luca. I'm calling you about a message.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Lascia il tuo messaggio dopo il segnale.
dialogue.translation: Leave your message after the tone.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ok, poi ti chiamo a casa. Ciao!
dialogue.translation: Okay, I'll call you at home later. Bye!

scenario: At the post office sending a package
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: feminine noun, envelope or small bag
masculine noun, form to fill out

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, devo spedire un pacco. Quanto costa?
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I have to send a package. How much does it cost?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Dipende dal peso. Mi dia il pacco, per favore.
dialogue.translation: It depends on the weight. Give me the package, please.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ecco. C'è anche una busta con documenti.
dialogue.translation: Here it is. There is also an envelope with documents.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Va bene. Il prezzo è venti euro. Deve riempire questo modulo.
dialogue.translation: All right. The price is twenty euros. You must fill out this form.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Grazie. Ho bisogno di qualcosa? ... No, faccio subito.
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Do I need anything? ... No, I'll do it right away.

key_phrases.translation: You must fill out this form

scenario: Describing your daily routine
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Used to express a daily repetition.
Pronominal verb, very common in routines.
Very frequent verb, used in 'fare colazione'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ogni giorno mi alzo alle sette e faccio colazione.
dialogue.translation: Every day I get up at seven and have breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: E dopo il pranzo, cosa fai?
dialogue.translation: And after lunch, what do you do?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Dopo pranzo torno a casa e riposo un po'.
dialogue.translation: After lunch I go back home and rest a bit.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: E la sera, ceni a casa?
dialogue.translation: And in the evening, do you have dinner at home?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sì, la cena è sempre a casa.
dialogue.translation: Yes, dinner is always at home.

scenario: Asking about opening hours
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Irregular verb, used for shops and establishments.
Feminine, often used to ask the opening time.
Pronominal form, less common but used for schedules.
Articulated preposition (da + le), used for schedules.
Articulated preposition (a + le), used for times.
Often followed by 'a' or 'alle' to indicate the end of a schedule.
Coordinating conjunction to introduce an opposition.
Structure to express a time range.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A che ora aprite oggi?
dialogue.translation: What time do you open today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Apriamo dalle 8 alle 12, ma chiudiamo per pranzo.
dialogue.translation: We open from 8 to 12, but we close for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E poi aprite di nuovo fino a che ora?
dialogue.translation: And then you open again until what time?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sì, riapriamo alle 15 e restiamo aperti fino alle 19.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we reopen at 15 and stay open until 19.

scenario: Choosing a dish from a menu
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Used to order or choose something.
Often used to say 'let's see' or 'let's look'.
It can also be a noun ('il bene') or an interjection.
Common preposition, also in compound dishes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vediamo il menu: cosa prendiamo?
dialogue.translation: Let's look at the menu: what are we having?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Non so, ma voglio carne o pesce con patate.
dialogue.translation: I don't know, but I want meat or fish with potatoes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bene, prendiamo carne con insalata?
dialogue.translation: Well, shall we have meat with salad?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sì, ma voglio vedere anche il pesce.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I also want to see the fish.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Va bene, prendiamo pesce per te e carne per me.
dialogue.translation: Okay, we'll have fish for you and meat for me.

scenario: At the bank for a simple transaction
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Italian

vocabulary.note: Often used with 'corrente' (current account) but here alone.
Bank card, often 'carta di credito' or 'bancomat'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, devo andare in banca per un semplice prelievo.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I have to go to the bank for a simple withdrawal.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hai già il conto qui?
dialogue.translation: Do you already have an account here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sì, ho la carta e i soldi sul conto.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have the card and the money in the account.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ma hai bisogno di un documento?
dialogue.translation: But do you need a document?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No, ho già tutto, grazie.
dialogue.translation: No, I already have everything, thanks.

key_phrases.translation: I have to go to the bank
